newsitem.title: USA: Tour finds healthy corn, soy in northern Indiana.
newsitem.headline: Tour finds healthy corn, soy in northern Indiana.

text.p: Corn and soybeans in northeast Indiana and northern Ohio appeared to be in average to above average condition, crop scouts said on one leg of the Professional Farmers of America Corn and Soybean Tour.
Five fields were scouted in northeast Indiana and five in northwest Ohio and all featured rich green plants, but plant development appeared to be less than expected.
"The beans are shorter than I expected and the plant population isn't quite as high , but beans can put on a lot of pods on short stems," said Rick Rottinghaus, a corn/soy farmer from Waterloo, Iowa.
One corn field had minor corn borer damage, but other fields were largely free of insect damage and disease.
The corn needs warm weather to boost development, which would help avoid crop damage should there be an early freeze.
"The biggest concern right now is a possible early freeze, the crop will to have to hustle," said Byron Jones, a corn and soybean farmer from McLean County, Ill.,
Soil moisture was adequate to abundant across Tuesday's leg of the tour.
The tour will advance through Indiana late Tuesday and enter Illinois Wednesday
